run: set -eu; command -v nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo 'vLLM needs an NVIDIA GPU and driver (nvidia-smi not found)' >&2; exit 1; }; cuda_major=$(nvidia-smi -q 2>/dev/null | awk -F' *: *' '/^CUDA (UMD )?Version/ {split($2, v, "."); print v[1]; exit}'); [ "${cuda_major:-0}" -ge 13 ] 2>/dev/null || { echo "vLLM needs an NVIDIA driver that supports CUDA 13 or newer (found: ${cuda_major:-none}). Update your NVIDIA driver and try again." >&2; exit 1; }; free_kb=$(df -Pk "$2" | awk 'NR==2 {print $4}'); [ "${free_kb:-0}" -ge 15728640 ] || { echo 'vLLM needs at least 15 GB of free disk space' >&2; exit 1; }; mkdir -p "$2/uv"; tar -xzf "$1" -C "$2/uv" --strip-components=1; export UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR="$2/python" UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-managed; "$2/uv/uv" venv --no-cache --python 3.12 "$2/venv"; "$2/uv/uv" pip install --no-cache --python "$2/venv/bin/python" "vllm==0.32.0"

list_models.description: List the models in the Hugging Face cache that vLLM could serve (complete downloads with a config, tokenizer and weights). Needs no running engine.

load_model.description: Serve a different model (params: {"model": "<Hugging Face id>"}). vLLM serves one model per process, so this saves the model into the launch arguments and restarts the engine on it; if the new model does not start, the previous one is restored.

unload_model.description: Eject the model vLLM is serving (params: {"model": "<id>"}). vLLM cannot drop its model and keep running, so this stops the engine, which frees all of its GPU memory. Load starts it again.

delete_model.description: Delete a downloaded model from the Hugging Face cache (params: {"model": "<org/name>"}). The model vLLM is set to serve is refused: switch to another model first.

pull_model.description: Download a model from Hugging Face into the shared cache (params: {"model": "<org/name>"}). Needs no running engine. Once downloaded it appears in list_models and can be served with load_model.

loaded_models.description: List the model this vLLM server is serving (it serves exactly one). This is what peers and the proxy are told it can answer for.
